sentences.translation: #The land of blank paper
The afternoon editors were at a time when only the roar of air conditioning and the friction of paper were floating.
MURAKAMI Saori spread a bunch of public relations materials at his desk and looked through the report of agricultural administration distributed by Kamige City this year.
A review of the feature story — that was the job this week.
On page 32, my finger stopped.
There was a very different tempo of procedures for the delisting of agricultural promotion areas.
Usually, it takes six months to decide to cancel the examination.
It should be a procedure to be reviewed by multiple institutions based on the law.
However, the area—the northern part of Kamige City, the 23nd site of the Osato area—was cancelled within 73 days of the application.
Saori confirmed the date twice.
"The 73th."
The numbers sounded even more strange when I spoke to them.
The reason was written.

The government has been working to create a new policy for farmers, and it has been said that the government will "approval of the government's decision to prioritize the revitalization of the local economy in light of the increase in farmland abandoned by the aging population. "
The grounds are written.
But the more you read, the less you know where the reasoning came from.
The next morning, Saori visited the Osato area.
The place where the rice fields were supposed to have been spread was already a cliché.
The red soil was exposed and the tires of heavy machinery ran vertically and horizontally.
A white pile of borders was struck at equal intervals, with a small seal on one of them.
Saori broke his knee and approached him.
It is printed as 'Towa-jiken.'
It was the name of a real estate company.
Saori used a smartphone to make a close-up of the seal, counting the surrounding piles, and grasping the approximate size of the compartment.
Near a hectare.
Housing development, commercial facilities — this is the size and location of both.
When he returned to the editorial office, he opened a search system for corporate registration.
Towa Landbuilding Co. , Ltd.
It was founded two years ago.
The president is Koreyuki Kurosawa.
The headquarters is located in the center of the city.
The capital is 20 million yen.

The government tried to examine the registration information regarding the transfer of ownership of the land, but it was necessary to go to a prefectural office to view the original book, which was recorded.
That will be tomorrow or later.
The problem was that there was no evidence.
It is not illegal to review early.
In the range of rules, speed is only a matter of discretion.
It is not unnatural for Towa-jiken to own land.
It is natural for real estate companies to have land.
For now, it may be just a coincidence of a date match — Saori told himself.
But still, the feeling of something sinking at the bottom of the stomach did not disappear.
"There must be some backdrop that permits are given so quickly."
I didn't say what I thought.
On the editorial office floor, Hiroki Suda ran a note to the notebook while calling.
The Koike desk is facing the display in a glass-covered private room at the back.
Nobody is looking at this.
Saori wrote in his notebook, '32 Ori, Towajiken, 73 days,' and then he wrote, 'Why?'
It’s unclear if this will be an article.
But it’s worth exploring — and that’s all.
She began planning the interview the next day.
The registration office of the prefecture, the city minutes, the report of the agricultural committee.
The twigs may be thin, but if you pull them, something may continue.
Outside the window, the autumn sun was beginning to tilt.
